title: Scan CLI, setup, download, install, doctor, dispatch, and maintenance tooling for missed shared-module adoption
scope: H31 tooling-surface scan across tools/setup/**, tools/download/**, tools/tooling/**, tools/dispatch/**, tools/analysis/**, tools/bench/**, tools/triage/**, plus related root-level tool scripts.

summary.overallAssessment: These tool surfaces already have a substantial shared layer under tools/shared plus a few src/shared runtime/platform helpers. The strongest missed-adoption cases are symlink-unsafe direct-execution guards still scattered across tool entrypoints, setup/bootstrap scripts that still carry bespoke Windows wrapper launching instead of converging on the shared subprocess wrapper path, and repeated runtime-env shaping across triage, analysis, setup, and bench scripts. Download and install surfaces are comparatively healthy: they already use shared CLI display, input parsing, download-utils, and json-utils and should mostly stay on that path.

highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: Tool scripts are frequently invoked through wrappers and generated launchers. Exact argv/url equality checks can silently skip execution under symlinks.
npm/cmd.exe wrapper handling is correctness-sensitive on Windows and recently produced real bugs elsewhere in the repo.

highestPriorityHotspots.category: runtime env shaping across tool surfaces
highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: Bench/setup/triage/analysis scripts repeatedly shape runtime env from config, and drift here changes real execution behavior.

hotspotMatrix.name: Symlink-unsafe direct-execution guards remain in tool entrypoints
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Replace exact process.argv[1] versus fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) checks with the shared direct-execution helper unless a script intentionally accepts basename-style wrapper invocation.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: This is the same bug class already fixed in other entrypoints. Using the shared helper removes repeated path-comparison logic and keeps tool launch behavior consistent.
testsToRequire: CLI or tool wrapper contract tests where entrypoint execution is user-facing
targeted symlink or shim launch regressions when a tool surface is moved to the helper

hotspotMatrix.name: Setup/bootstrap scripts still carry bespoke Windows wrapper launching
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Use the shared Windows wrapper resolution path and shared command-running helpers for setup/bootstrap flows, leaving only script-specific command selection local.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: The wrapper and shell-fallback behavior has already been fixed centrally. Re-implementing it in setup scripts reintroduces the same Windows fragility.
testsToRequire: existing windows-wrapper and bootstrap contract tests
cross-platform setup smoke tests where wrapper selection changes

hotspotMatrix.name: Runtime env shaping repeats across setup, triage, analysis, and bench tools
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Keep using the current shared runtime-config/env helpers and reduce raw process.env shaping to script-local payload overrides only.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These tools do need local env injection, but not their own independent config-to-env policy. Shared runtime env shaping is already available and proven.
testsToRequire: bench and triage runtime env inheritance tests
setup/tooling env contract tests where NODE_OPTIONS or cache-root shaping can drift

hotspotMatrix.name: Tooling install/uninstall/download surfaces already share the right CLI and IO helpers
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Treat this as a mostly healthy shared-adoption area. Prefer targeted helper expansion over refactoring these scripts into a new abstraction.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These surfaces already demonstrate the intended tools/shared usage pattern. Additional hoisting would mostly move script semantics around without reducing much drift.

hotspotMatrix.name: Bench/report helper adoption is mixed but should stay selective
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Keep sharing low-level CLI/text/JSON helpers, but leave benchmark semantics and artifact-shaping logic local unless duplication is proven substantial.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: Bench scripts often differ mainly in workload semantics, not in low-level helper needs. Over-consolidation would reduce debuggability without much drift payoff.

mappings.problemSurface: Windows wrapper launching in setup/bootstrap tools
Runtime env shaping in setup/triage/bench/analysis tools

localExceptions.reasonToRemainMostlyLocal: Already follows the healthy tools/shared pattern and still needs script-specific extension archive semantics.
Same rationale as extension downloads: shared download/input/json helpers are already in place.
Installer plan semantics are tooling-specific; the right cleanup is helper reuse, not flattening the whole script.
Uninstall policy and safety checks are tooling-specific even when path/CLI helpers are shared.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainSelective: Bench scripts should share low-level helper primitives, but not be over-consolidated into generic benchmark abstractions without clear duplicate evidence.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainPartlyLocal: Browser-opening behavior and map-serve UX are analysis-tool specific even if wrapper/env setup should converge.

recommendedFollowUps.why: Editor and integration surfaces should absorb the same direct-execution/runtime/bootstrap cleanup patterns where they appear again.
If setup/bootstrap/tooling wrapper cleanup still feels fragmented after H31 adoption, formalize a stronger shared subprocess/toolchain helper family.
If report-writing and small JSON/file IO duplication continues to appear in benches and tooling, capture it in the filesystem/JSON/persistence helper issue.
